grammar.title: First…, then… with 先…然后/再…
grammar.pattern: 先 + Verb 1 ，然后 / 再 + Verb 2
grammar.explain: Use 先 for the first action and 然后 ('afterwards') or 再 ('then') for the next one. 然后 starts a new clause and can stand at the beginning of it; 再 must come right before the verb. You can also combine them: 然后再…

grammar.title: 就 (early) vs 才 (late)
grammar.pattern: Time + 就 + Verb + 了 ／ Time + 才 + Verb
grammar.explain: After a time expression, 就 shows that something happens earlier or more easily than expected, and the sentence usually ends with 了. 才 shows that something happens later than expected ('not until'), and the sentence does not take 了.

examples.zh: 他 十 点 才 起床 。

grammar.title: As soon as: 一…就…
grammar.pattern: Subject + 一 + Verb 1 ，就 + Verb 2
grammar.explain: 一…就… means 'as soon as A happens, B happens'. 一 goes before the first verb and 就 before the second. If the two actions have different subjects, each subject goes before its own 一 or 就.

reading.title: 我的一天
reading.zh: 我叫王明，在一家公司工作。我每天早上六点半起床，先洗澡、刷牙，然后吃早饭。我习惯早上喝咖啡。七点一刻我从家里出去，坐公共汽车去公司，二十分钟就到了。我一般七点五十到公司，很少迟到。中午我在公司吃饭，吃完以后休息一会儿。下午五点半下班，我一回家就开始做饭。吃完饭以后，我经常去跑步。晚上我十一点睡觉，睡觉以前总是看一会儿书。星期六和星期天我九点才起床。
reading.en: My name is Wang Ming and I work at a company. Every morning I get up at six thirty. First I take a shower and brush my teeth, then I have breakfast. I'm used to drinking coffee in the morning. At a quarter past seven I leave home and take the bus to the office; it gets there in twenty minutes. I usually arrive at seven fifty, and I'm rarely late. At noon I eat at the office and rest for a while after eating. I finish work at five thirty, and as soon as I get home I start cooking. After dinner I often go running. I go to bed at eleven, and before going to sleep I always read for a while. On Saturdays and Sundays I don't get up until nine.

grammar.title: Same or different: 跟…一样
grammar.pattern: A + 跟 + B + 一样 (+ Adjective) ／ A + 跟 + B + 不一样
grammar.explain: A 跟 B 一样 means 'A is the same as B'. Add an adjective after 一样 to say 'A is as … as B'. Put 不 before 一样 for the negative.

examples.zh: 我 跟 我 哥哥 一样 高 。
examples.en: I'm as tall as my older brother.

examples.zh: 我 的 手机 跟 你 的 不 一样 。

grammar.title: Comparing with 比, 更 and 没有
grammar.pattern: A + 比 + B + (更/还) + Adjective (+ 多了) ／ A + 没有 + B + (那么) + Adjective
grammar.explain: A 比 B + adjective means 'A is more … than B'. Put 更 or 还 before the adjective for 'even more'. Never use 很 or 非常 in a 比 sentence; to say 'much more', add 多了 after the adjective. To say 'A is not as … as B', use A 没有 B (那么) + adjective.

examples.zh: 他 很 高 ， 他 弟弟 更 高 。
examples.en: He's tall, and his younger brother is even taller.

examples.zh: 今天 比 昨天 冷 多 了 。
examples.en: Today is much colder than yesterday.

examples.zh: 我 没有 我 哥哥 那么 高 。
examples.en: I'm not as tall as my older brother.

grammar.title: Extremely: Adjective + 极了
grammar.pattern: Adjective + 极 + 了
grammar.explain: 极了 after an adjective means 'extremely' or 'really, really'. It is common in speech and always comes after the adjective, never before it. Don't add 很 in front.

grammar.title: Result complements: 完, 好, 懂, 错, 到, 清楚
grammar.pattern: Verb + Result (+ 了) ／ 没 + Verb + Result
grammar.explain: A second word after the verb tells you the result of the action: 做完 'finish doing', 写好 'finish writing (properly)', 听懂 'understand by listening', 写错 'write wrongly', 找到 'find', 看清楚 'see clearly'. Use 了 when the result has happened and 没 (not 不) for the negative.

grammar.title: How an action is done: Adjective + 地 + Verb
grammar.pattern: (很 / 非常) + Adjective + 地 + Verb
grammar.explain: 地 (pronounced de) turns an adjective into an adverb, like English '-ly'. It goes between the adjective and the verb. Two-syllable adjectives such as 认真 or 努力 usually take 很 or 非常 in front; reduplicated adjectives like 慢慢 also go well with 地.

grammar.title: How well something is done: Verb + 得 + Adjective
grammar.pattern: (Object +) Verb + 得 + (很) + Adjective
grammar.explain: To comment on how well someone does something, put 得 after the verb and an adjective after 得. If there is an object, put it before the verb (or repeat the verb: 写字写得…). The negative puts 不 before the adjective: 写得不好.

reading.title: 李月的汉语成绩
reading.zh: 李月是三年级的学生。她学习非常努力，每天晚上都认真地复习。她最喜欢数学，觉得数学题很容易，但是她觉得汉语比较难。汉语的词语很多，句子也不简单。上个星期考试，她的汉语成绩不太好，她很不高兴。老师告诉她：“你每天练习写字，多读书，成绩就会提高。”李月明白了老师的意思，现在她每天都练习写字半个小时。这次考试，她的成绩比上次好多了。老师和同学们都为她高兴。
reading.en: Li Yue is a third-grade student. She studies very hard and reviews carefully every evening. Her favorite subject is math; she finds math problems easy, but she thinks Chinese is rather difficult. Chinese has lots of words and expressions, and the sentences aren't simple either. Last week there was an exam, and her Chinese grade wasn't very good. She was very unhappy. Her teacher told her: “Practice writing characters every day and read more, and your grades will improve.” Li Yue understood what the teacher meant, and now she practices writing characters for half an hour every day. In this exam, her results were much better than last time. Her teacher and classmates are all happy for her.

grammar.title: Putting things somewhere: 把 + Object + Verb + 在/到/给
grammar.pattern: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + 在 / 到 / 给 + Place / Person
grammar.explain: 把 moves the object in front of the verb so you can say what you do to it and where it ends up. It is used for definite things (this book, the fridge). With 放在, 搬到 or 拿给, the place or person comes after the verb phrase. The verb can never stand alone after 把.

grammar.title: Getting something done: 把 + Object + Verb + Result/了
grammar.pattern: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + Result Complement / 了
grammar.explain: 把 is also used to say what result an action has on the object: 打扫干净 'clean until clean', 做完 'finish doing', 关了 'turn off'. The negative 没 or 别 goes before 把, not before the verb.

grammar.title: Describing a state with 着
grammar.pattern: Verb + 着 ／ Place + Verb + 着 + Object
grammar.explain: 着 after a verb shows that a state continues: 开着 'is on / is open'. It also describes what is placed somewhere: 桌子上放着… 'on the table there is (lying)…'. The negative is 没 + Verb + 着.

grammar.title: The passive with 被
grammar.pattern: Receiver + 被 + (Doer) + Verb + Complement / 了
grammar.explain: In a 被 sentence the thing that is affected comes first, and the doer (if mentioned) comes after 被. It is mostly used for things that happen to you, often unpleasant ones. Like 把, the verb needs something after it, such as 了 or a result (拿走, 用坏). If you don't know who did it, use 人 or leave the doer out.

grammar.title: Experience 过 vs completed 了
grammar.pattern: Verb + 过 (ever done) ／ Verb + 了 (done, at a specific time)
grammar.explain: 过 after a verb says that you have had the experience at some time in the past: 'have ever done'. Its negative is 没 + Verb + 过. 了 says that an action was completed, often at a specific time: 'did'. Compare 我去过北京 (I've been to Beijing) with 我昨天去了北京 (I went to Beijing yesterday).

reading.en: Yesterday was a really strange day. In the morning my phone broke, so I didn't get up until seven thirty. I was in a hurry and left without eating breakfast. On the bus, I suddenly noticed that my wallet wasn't in my bag. Had someone taken it? I thought for a moment and then remembered that I had left it on the table at home. In the afternoon I went to the library to borrow a dictionary, but someone had already borrowed it. On the way home, I ran into a former classmate. He bought me a coffee and we talked about lots of things from the old days. That was the happiest moment of my day.

grammar.title: Simple directional complements: Verb + 来/去
grammar.pattern: Verb + 来 (towards the speaker) ／ Verb + 去 (away from the speaker)
grammar.explain: 来 and 去 after a verb show the direction of a movement: 来 means towards the speaker, 去 means away from the speaker. Common combinations are 进来 'come in', 出去 'go out', 回来 'come back', 上来 'come up', 下去 'go down'. A place word goes before 来/去: 回家来, 进教室去.

grammar.title: Compound directional complements
grammar.pattern: Verb + 上/下/进/出/回/过 + 来/去
grammar.explain: Add 上 'up', 下 'down', 进 'in', 出 'out', 回 'back' or 过 'over' before 来/去 to describe a movement more exactly: 走下来 'walk down (towards me)', 走过去 'walk over (away from me)', 拿出来 'take out'. The first verb tells you how the movement happens.

grammar.title: Giving directions with 往 and 离
grammar.pattern: 往 + Direction + 走 ／ A + 离 + B + Distance
grammar.explain: 往 means 'towards': 往东走 'walk east', 一直往前走 'go straight ahead'. 离 tells you the distance between two places: 我家离地铁站五百米 'my home is 500 meters from the subway station'. Use 远 or 近 after 离 B for 'far' or 'near'.

reading.zh: 上个星期六，我第一次去朋友小张家。小张给我打电话，告诉我怎么走：“你先坐地铁到东门站，从二号口出来。然后一直往南走，经过一个医院，过了马路就到了。我家就在一个商店和一个饭馆中间。”我从地铁站出来以后，不知道哪边是南边，就往西走了。走了二十分钟，我还没找到。我给小张打电话，他骑自行车来接我。他家离地铁站很近，是我走错了。
reading.en: Last Saturday I went to my friend Xiao Zhang's home for the first time. Xiao Zhang called me and told me how to get there: “First take the subway to Dongmen Station and come out of Exit 2. Then go straight south, past a hospital, and once you cross the road you're there. My place is right between a shop and a restaurant.” When I came out of the subway station, I didn't know which way was south, so I walked west. After twenty minutes I still hadn't found it. I called Xiao Zhang, and he rode his bike over to pick me up. His home is very close to the station; I had just gone the wrong way.

grammar.title: Potential complements: Verb + 得/不 + Result
grammar.pattern: Verb + 得 + Result (can) ／ Verb + 不 + Result (can't)
grammar.explain: Put 得 or 不 between a verb and its result to say whether the result is possible: 吃得完 'can finish eating', 吃不完 'can't finish eating', 听得懂 'can understand', 听不懂 'can't understand'. This is the most natural way to say 'can't' when circumstances stop you. To ask, use 吗 or Verb得…Verb不…: 听得懂听不懂？

grammar.title: Can or can't manage: Verb + 得了/不了
grammar.pattern: Verb + 得了 (liǎo) ／ Verb + 不了 (liǎo)
grammar.explain: 了 pronounced liǎo after 得 or 不 means 'be able to manage'. 吃不了 means 'can't eat (that much)', 去不了 means 'can't go (because something prevents it)'. A second 了 at the end of the sentence means 'any more': 吃不了了 'I can't eat any more'.

grammar.explain: 又…又… joins two qualities or states that are true at the same time: 'both … and …'. The two parts should both be positive or both be negative in feeling.

reading.zh: 安娜第一次来中国的时候，不会用筷子，吃饭吃得很慢。中国菜又好吃又便宜，但是菜单上的字她都看不懂，服务员的问题她也听不懂，所以她每次都点面条。一碗面条十块钱，又好吃又能吃饱。现在她已经会用筷子了，也看得懂菜单了。她经常去学校旁边的一家小饭馆，那里的菜很新鲜，服务员都认识她。吃完饭，她还喜欢买一点水果，香蕉、葡萄她都喜欢。她说：“在中国，我每天都吃得很饱！”
reading.en: When Anna first came to China, she couldn't use chopsticks and ate very slowly. Chinese food is delicious and cheap, but she couldn't read anything on the menu or understand the waiters' questions, so she ordered noodles every time. A bowl of noodles cost ten yuan; it was tasty and filling. Now she can use chopsticks and read the menu. She often goes to a small restaurant next to the school, where the food is very fresh and all the waiters know her. After eating, she likes to buy some fruit; she likes both bananas and grapes. She says: “In China, I eat until I'm full every day!”

grammar.pattern: Subject + 越来越 + Adjective / Verb (+ 了)
grammar.explain: 越来越 means 'more and more' and shows a change over time. It goes right before the adjective or verb, and the sentence often ends with 了. Do not add 很 or 非常 after 越来越.

reading.title: 北京的四个季节
reading.zh: 北京有四个季节：春天、夏天、秋天和冬天。春天经常刮风，有时候风很大，但是花都开了，非常漂亮。夏天很热，经常下雨，出去的时候包里最好放一把伞。秋天是北京最好的季节，不冷也不热，天特别蓝，晚上的月亮也很漂亮。冬天很冷，有时候零下十几度，但是房间里不冷。下雪的时候，北京多么漂亮啊！但是很多北京人都说，北京的秋天越来越短了。
reading.en: Beijing has four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. In spring it's often windy, and sometimes the wind is very strong, but all the flowers are in bloom and it's very beautiful. Summer is hot and it rains a lot, so it's best to keep an umbrella in your bag when you go out. Autumn is Beijing's best season: it's neither cold nor hot, the sky is especially blue, and the moon at night is lovely too. Winter is cold, sometimes more than ten degrees below zero, but it isn't cold indoors. When it snows, Beijing is so beautiful! But many people in Beijing say that autumn there is getting shorter and shorter.

grammar.title: If …, then …: 如果…就…
grammar.pattern: 如果 + Condition ，(Subject +) 就 + Result
grammar.explain: 如果 introduces a condition ('if') and 就 introduces the result ('then'). 如果 can come before or after the subject of the first clause; 就 always comes after the subject of the second clause, right before the verb. In speech, 的话 is often added at the end of the condition.

grammar.title: As long as …: 只要…就…
grammar.pattern: 只要 + Condition ，(Subject +) 就 + Result
grammar.explain: 只要…就… means 'as long as A, then B': A is enough to make B happen. It sounds more encouraging than 如果. On its own, 只 means 'only' and goes right before the verb.

reading.title: 爸爸的身体
reading.zh: 我爸爸工作很忙，以前很少锻炼。他每天在公司坐八个小时，回家以后就看电视。去年冬天，他感冒了好几次，腿和脚也经常疼。我们都很担心他。医生给他检查了身体，说：“你的身体没有大问题，但是你需要多锻炼。如果你每天走路半个小时，身体就会好很多。”从那以后，爸爸每天早上都去跑步，星期六还跟朋友一起去游泳。他还少喝啤酒，多吃水果。现在爸爸很少感冒，我们都放心了。爸爸经常说：“只要每天锻炼，身体就会越来越健康。”
reading.en: My dad is very busy at work, and he used to exercise very little. He sat at the office for eight hours a day and watched TV after he got home. Last winter he caught several colds, and his legs and feet often hurt too. We were all very worried about him. The doctor gave him a checkup and said: “There's nothing seriously wrong, but you need to exercise more. If you walk for half an hour every day, you'll be much healthier.” Since then, Dad has gone running every morning, and on Saturdays he goes swimming with friends. He also drinks less beer and eats more fruit. Now he rarely catches colds, and we're no longer worried. Dad often says: “As long as you exercise every day, you'll get healthier and healthier.”

grammar.title: Except / besides: 除了…以外
grammar.pattern: 除了 A (以外)，B + 还 / 也 + … ／ 除了 A (以外)，都 + …
grammar.explain: 除了 A 以外 followed by 还 or 也 means 'besides A, also …' (A is included). Followed by 都 it means 'except A, all …' (A is left out). 以外 can be dropped in speech.

grammar.title: Two kinds of 'or': 还是 and 或者
grammar.pattern: A 还是 B ？(question) ／ A 或者 B (statement)
grammar.explain: Use 还是 to ask someone to choose: 'Do you want A or B?'. Use 或者 in statements, when either choice is fine: 'A or B, either is OK'. A sentence with 还是 is already a question, so it doesn't take 吗.

grammar.title: Reduplication: 看看, 想想, 好好
grammar.pattern: Verb + Verb (AA / ABAB) ／ Adjective + Adjective
grammar.explain: Repeating a verb makes it sound short, light and polite: 看看 'take a look', 想想 'think it over', 休息休息 'have a little rest'. Repeating a one-syllable adjective makes it more vivid: 好好 'properly', 慢慢 'slowly'. Two-syllable adjectives repeat as AABB, for example 高高兴兴.

reading.title: 跟妈妈买衣服
reading.zh: 星期天下午，我和妈妈去商店买衣服。妈妈想给我买一条裙子，但是我更喜欢穿裤子。商店里的衣服很多，有红的、白的、黑的，还有黄的。我试了好几条裤子，才找到一条又便宜又舒服的。除了裤子以外，妈妈还给我买了一件衬衫和一双鞋，一共花了六百多块钱。妈妈问我：“你满意了吧？”我说：“满意极了！”然后我们去超市买了一些水果和面包。在超市里，妈妈问我：“晚上吃面条还是米饭？”我说：“面条或者米饭都可以。”
reading.en: On Sunday afternoon, Mom and I went to the shops to buy clothes. Mom wanted to buy me a skirt, but I prefer wearing trousers. The shop had lots of clothes: red, white, black and yellow ones too. I tried on several pairs of trousers before I found a pair that was both cheap and comfortable. Besides the trousers, Mom also bought me a shirt and a pair of shoes. Altogether we spent over six hundred yuan. Mom asked me: “Are you happy now?” I said: “Very happy!” Then we went to the supermarket and bought some fruit and bread. In the supermarket Mom asked me: “Shall we have noodles or rice tonight?” I said: “Noodles or rice, either is fine.”

grammar.title: Being interested: 对…感兴趣
grammar.pattern: A + 对 + B + (很) 感兴趣 ／ A + 对 + B + 没有兴趣
grammar.explain: To say that you are interested in something, put 对 + the thing before 感兴趣. Adverbs like 很 or 特别 go before 感兴趣. The negative is 对…不感兴趣 or 对…没有兴趣.

grammar.title: Doing two things at once: 一边…一边…
grammar.pattern: Subject + 一边 + Verb 1 ，一边 + Verb 2
grammar.explain: 一边…一边… means that someone does two actions at the same time. Each 一边 goes right before a verb. The subject comes only once, at the beginning.

examples.zh: 他 一边 听 音乐 ， 一边 做 作业 。

grammar.title: Not only … but also …: 不但…而且…
grammar.pattern: Subject + 不但 + A ，而且 (+ 还/也) + B
grammar.explain: 不但 A，而且 B means 'not only A, but also B'. B usually adds something stronger or extra. If both parts have the same subject, put it before 不但. 还 or 也 is often added after 而且.

reading.zh: 我叫大卫，在北京学习汉语。我的爱好很多：听音乐、画画、爬山，还有玩电子游戏。周末我经常一边听音乐，一边画画。去年我参加了学校的画画比赛，老师们都说我画得不错。我对中国音乐也很感兴趣，所以我的中国朋友小李每个星期都教我唱歌。上个月，我们一起在学校表演了一个节目，大家都很喜欢。我还喜欢爬山，北京附近有很多地方可以爬山，我的照相机里有很多爬山的照片。我觉得有爱好的人不但每天都很快乐，而且身体也很健康。
reading.en: My name is David and I'm studying Chinese in Beijing. I have lots of hobbies: listening to music, painting, hiking and playing video games. At weekends I often paint while listening to music. Last year I entered the school painting competition, and the teachers all said I painted well. I'm also very interested in Chinese music, so my Chinese friend Xiao Li teaches me songs every week. Last month we performed together at school, and everyone loved it. I also like hiking. There are lots of places to hike near Beijing, and my camera is full of hiking photos. I think people with hobbies are not only happy every day, but healthier too.

grammar.title: In order to: 为了
grammar.pattern: 为了 + Purpose ，Subject + Verb ……
grammar.explain: 为了 introduces the purpose of an action: 'in order to' or 'for the sake of'. The 为了 phrase normally comes first, followed by a comma and the main clause that says what is done.

examples.zh: 为了 学习 汉语 ， 他 来 了 中国 。

grammar.title: About, concerning: 关于
grammar.pattern: 关于 + Topic ，…… ／ 关于 + Topic + 的 + Noun
grammar.explain: 关于 introduces a topic: 'about' or 'concerning'. It can start a sentence (关于这件事情，……) or describe a noun with 的 (关于中国的书 'a book about China'). Unlike English, a 关于 phrase never comes after the verb at the end of the sentence.

grammar.title: Stressing details of the past: 是…的
grammar.pattern: Subject + (是) + Time / Place / Manner + Verb + 的
grammar.explain: When both speakers already know that something happened, 是…的 is used to focus on when, where, how or with whom it happened. 是 goes before the detail you want to stress, and 的 goes after the verb. 是 can be dropped in speech, but 的 cannot.

reading.title: 我的新工作
reading.zh: 我是去年九月来这家公司工作的。为了找到这个工作，我准备了很长时间。我们公司主要卖电脑和手机。我的经理姓张，他对工作要求很高，但是人很好。我的同事都很年轻，也很聪明，我们经常一起吃饭。开始工作的时候，我遇到了很多问题，每天都很着急。同事们教我怎么解决问题，我也每天认真地学习。上个月，经理给了我一个机会，让我一个人完成一个重要的工作。那几天我每天都工作到晚上九点，终于完成了。在会议上，经理说我做得很好。我很高兴我选择了这家公司。
reading.en: I came to work at this company last September. I spent a long time preparing to get this job. Our company mainly sells computers and phones. My manager's surname is Zhang. He's very demanding about work, but he's a nice person. My colleagues are all young and smart, and we often eat together. When I started, I ran into lots of problems and felt anxious every day. My colleagues taught me how to solve problems, and I studied hard every day. Last month the manager gave me a chance to complete an important job on my own. For those few days I worked until nine every evening, and I finally finished it. At the meeting, the manager said I had done a great job. I'm really glad I chose this company.

grammar.title: Although …, (but) …: 虽然…但是…
grammar.pattern: 虽然 + A ，但是 + (Subject +) B
grammar.explain: 虽然 means 'although'. Unlike English, Chinese normally keeps 但是 ('but') in the second clause as well. 虽然 can come before or after the subject of the first clause. 还是 ('still') is often added in the second clause.

examples.zh: 虽然 他 很 忙 ， 但是 他 经常 给 我 打电话 。

grammar.title: Even: 连…都/也…
grammar.pattern: 连 + Noun / Phrase + 都 / 也 + Verb
grammar.explain: 连 A 都 B means 'even A does B': it points to an extreme or surprising example. 都 or 也 must follow, right before the verb. It is often used with a negative: 连…都没有 'not even …'.

grammar.title: Thinking wrongly: 以为 vs 认为
grammar.pattern: Subject + 以为 + Clause (but in fact …)
grammar.explain: 以为 means 'thought (wrongly)': what you believed turned out not to be true. 认为 simply gives your opinion. A sentence with 以为 is often followed by 其实 ('actually') to give the real situation.

reading.title: 热情的张阿姨
reading.zh: 我搬到这里以后，认识了邻居张阿姨。张阿姨六十多岁了，对人非常热情。虽然她已经不工作了，但是每天都很忙：早上去锻炼身体，下午去学校接孩子。她很关心别人，连楼里每家人的名字她都记得。上个月我感冒了，一个人在家，很难过。张阿姨知道以后，每天都给我送饭，还经常来照顾我。我想给她钱，她不同意，说：“你别给我钱，我们是邻居！”感冒好了以后，我买了一个礼物送给她。现在我们的关系就像一家人一样。
reading.en: After I moved here, I got to know my neighbor, Auntie Zhang. Auntie Zhang is in her sixties and is incredibly warm towards people. Although she's retired, she's busy every day: in the morning she goes to exercise, and in the afternoon she picks up the children from school. She really cares about others; she even remembers the names of everyone in the building. Last month I caught a cold and was at home alone, feeling miserable. When Auntie Zhang found out, she brought me food every day and often came to look after me. I wanted to give her money, but she refused and said: “Don't give me money, we're neighbors!” After I got better, I bought her a present. Now we're just like family.

grammar.title: From someone's point of view: 对…来说

grammar.explain: 对…来说 means 'for …' or 'as far as … is concerned'. It introduces whose point of view the rest of the sentence describes. It usually comes at the start of the sentence, followed by a comma.

grammar.title: Both … and …: 既…又…

grammar.explain: 既 A 又 B means 'both A and B'. It is similar to 又…又… but sounds a little more formal. A and B are usually adjectives or verb phrases of the same kind.

grammar.explain: To say 'not even one' or 'not at all', put 一 + measure word before 也 or 都 and a negative verb. With adjectives, use 一点也不: 一点也不累 'not tired at all'.

reading.title: 安娜过中秋节
reading.zh: 安娜来中国已经一年了。她很喜欢中国文化，一直想多了解一下中国人的节日。去年九月，她的朋友小李请她去家里过中秋节。中秋节是中国很重要的节日，这一天，家里人都要回家见面。小李的奶奶给安娜讲了一个关于月亮的故事。虽然有的地方安娜听不懂，但是她很喜欢这个故事。晚上，大家坐在一起，一边吃东西一边看月亮。对安娜来说，这是她第一次在中国人家里过中秋节。她觉得这个节日既有意思又让人快乐。过去她只在书上读过关于中国的故事，现在她觉得自己真的开始了解中国了。
reading.en: Anna has been in China for a year now. She loves Chinese culture and has always wanted to learn more about Chinese festivals. Last September, her friend Xiao Li invited her home to celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival. The Mid-Autumn Festival is a very important holiday in China; on this day, families get together at home. Xiao Li's grandma told Anna a story about the moon. Although there were parts Anna couldn't understand, she loved the story. In the evening everyone sat together, eating and looking at the moon. For Anna, it was the first time she had celebrated the Mid-Autumn Festival in a Chinese home. She found the festival both interesting and joyful. In the past she had only read stories about China in books; now she feels she has really started to understand China.

grammar.title: Only if …: 只有…才…
grammar.pattern: 只有 + Condition ，(Subject +) 才 + Result
grammar.explain: 只有 A 才 B means 'only if A, will B happen': A is the one necessary condition. Compare 只要…就… ('as long as'), where A is enough. 才 comes after the subject of the second clause, right before the verb.

grammar.title: Rhetorical questions: 不是…吗？ and 谁…？
grammar.pattern: 不是 + Statement + 吗 ？ ／ 谁 + 不/都 + Verb ？
grammar.explain: A rhetorical question isn't asking for information; it stresses something the speaker thinks is obvious. 你不是说…吗？ means 'Didn't you say …?' (and the speaker is surprised or annoyed). 谁不会？ means 'Who can't?', in other words 'everyone can'.

grammar.title: Causing a result: 使 / 让
grammar.pattern: A + 使 / 让 + B + Adjective / Verb
grammar.explain: 使 means 'to make' or 'to cause': A makes B feel or become something. 使 sounds more formal and is common in writing; in speech 让 is more common. B is followed by an adjective or verb describing the result.

reading.title: 我们城市的变化
reading.zh: 我在这个城市住了二十年了，这些年城市的变化非常大。过去这里只有几条街道，几乎没有高楼；现在高楼越来越多，地铁也越来越多，去哪里都很方便。人们几乎每天都上网，用手机买东西、看新闻。但是城市大了，车也多了，环境比过去差了。河里的鱼越来越少，树上也几乎看不到鸟了。为了使城市的环境更好，最近几年，城市里出现了很多新公园和花园，河边也种了很多树。现在，河里又有鱼了，树上的鸟也多了。我打算以后一直住在这里。我相信，只有大家都关心环境，我们的城市才会越来越漂亮。
reading.en: I've lived in this city for twenty years, and it has changed enormously in that time. In the past there were only a few streets and almost no tall buildings; now there are more and more high-rises and more and more subway lines, so it's convenient to get anywhere. People go online almost every day, using their phones to shop and read the news. But as the city grew, the number of cars grew too, and the environment became worse than before. There were fewer and fewer fish in the river, and you could hardly see any birds in the trees. To make the city's environment better, many new parks and gardens have appeared in recent years, and lots of trees have been planted along the river. Now there are fish in the river again, and more birds in the trees. I plan to keep living here. I believe that only if everyone cares about the environment will our city become more and more beautiful.
